Coconut Eggnog

Served at: Tiki Christmas at Pearl Harbor

Serves 6Prep 15 minCook 10 min

Coconut Eggnog is a tropical twist on the classic holiday drink, blending creamy coconut flavors with traditional eggnog spices. It is a festive favorite at Tiki Christmas celebrations at Pearl Harbor, evoking island warmth and holiday cheer.

Ingredients

  • 4 large eggs
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 cups (480 ml) whole milk
  • 1 cup (240 ml) coconut milk
  • 1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) dark rum or spiced rum (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, plus more for garnish
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Method

  1. In a large mixing bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar together until the mixture is smooth and pale.
  2. In a medium saucepan, combine the milk, coconut milk, heavy cream, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
  3. Heat the milk mixture over medium heat until it is hot but not boiling, stirring occasionally.
  4. Slowly temper the egg mixture by adding about 1/2 cup of the hot milk mixture to the eggs while whisking constantly.
  5. Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining milk mixture.
  6. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens slightly and reaches about 160°F (71°C), about 5-7 minutes. Do not boil.
  7. Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla extract and rum, if using.
  8. Let the eggnog cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
  9. Serve chilled, garnished with a sprinkle of freshly grated nutmeg.

Tips

  • For a non-alcoholic version, omit the rum and add a bit more vanilla or coconut extract for extra flavor.
  • Use fresh nutmeg for the best aromatic garnish.
  • If you prefer a thicker eggnog, you can whisk in an additional egg yolk during the tempering step.
